es.summary: Pérdida progresiva de la capacidad renal para filtrar sangre, eliminar desechos y regular líquidos y electrolitos. Requiere manejo de sustitución (diálisis o trasplante) y control de complicaciones.
key_points: Disminución del filtrado glomerular (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Retención de agua y electrolitos → edema e hipertensión
Acumulación de urea y creatinina → síntomas de uremia
Alteraciones óseas por desequilibrio de calcio‑fosfato

pathophysiology: Daño a nefronas → pérdida de filtración, reabsorción y secreción
Disminuye la tasa de filtrado glomerular (TFG) y aumenta BUN y creatinina
Retención de Na⁺ y agua eleva la presión arterial
Acumulación de desechos nitrogenados produce uremia
risk_factors: Uso prolongado de AINEs o nefrotoxinas
signs_symptoms: Disminución del volumen urinario o anuria
treatment: Control estricto de presión arterial (IECA o ARA II)
Diuréticos de asa (furosemida) para manejo de edema
Restricción de Na⁺, K⁺, fósforo y líquidos según indicación
Diálisis (hemodiálisis o peritoneal) o trasplante renal
nursing_care: Evaluar peso diario y balance I/O cada 8 h
Monitorear presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y signos de sobrecarga de líquidos
Controlar laboratorio de BUN, creatinina, electrolitos y hemoglobina
Inspeccionar piel y mucosas por prurito o úlceras
Preparar al paciente para sesiones de diálisis y observar accesos
patient_teaching: Dieta baja en sodio (<2 g/día) y potasio según nivel sérico
Limitar ingesta de líquidos según prescripción (ej. 1.5 L/día)
Tomar medicamentos antihipertensivos y eritropoyetina según indicación
Importancia de asistencia regular a diálisis o seguimiento trasplante

outcomes: Balance hídrico: peso estable ±0.5 kg en 48 h
Edema reducido a nivel leve en 72 h

interventions.action: Registrar peso y balance I/O cada 8 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios tempranos en la retención de líquidos

interventions.action: Evaluar edema (pitting) y registrar escala
interventions.rationale: Monitorea la gravedad de la sobrecarga de líquidos

interventions.action: Administrar furosemida según orden y observar respuesta
interventions.rationale: Diurético de asa favorece la eliminación de exceso de Na⁺ y agua

interventions.action: Elevar piernas del paciente cuando sea seguro
interventions.rationale: Facilita el retorno venoso y disminuye edema periférico

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre restricción de sodio y líquidos
interventions.rationale: Reduce la ingesta que contribuye a la retención

outcomes: Na⁺ y K⁺ séricos dentro de rangos normales (Na⁺ 135‑145 mEq/L, K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) en 72 h

interventions.action: Monitorear electrolitos séricos y gases arteriales cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta alteraciones tempranas y permite intervención oportuna

interventions.action: Evaluar signos neurológicos (confusión, debilidad muscular)
interventions.rationale: Los desequilibrios electrolíticos pueden manifestarse neurológicamente

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de calcio o fosfato según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Corrige desequilibrios específicos y previene complicaciones óseas

interventions.action: Reforzar educación dietética baja en potasio y fósforo
interventions.rationale: Controla la ingesta que afecta los niveles séricos

interventions.action: Ajustar medicación antihipertensiva (IECA/ARA II) según labs
interventions.rationale: Estos fármacos pueden elevar K⁺ y requerir ajuste

en.summary: Progressive loss of kidney function to filter blood, eliminate waste, and regulate fluids and electrolytes. Requires replacement therapy (dialysis or transplant) and management of complications.
key_points: Decreased glomerular filtration rate (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m²)
Water and electrolyte retention → edema and hypertension
Accumulation of urea and creatinine → uremic symptoms

pathophysiology: Damage to nephrons → loss of filtration, reabsorption, and secretion
Reduces glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and increases BUN and creatinine
Retention of Na⁺ and water raises blood pressure
Accumulation of nitrogenous waste produces uremia
risk_factors: Prolonged use of NSAIDs or nephrotoxins
treatment: Strict blood pressure control (ACE inhibitor or ARB)
Restriction of Na⁺, K⁺, phosphorus, and fluids as indicated
Dialysis (hemodialysis or peritoneal) or kidney transplant
nursing_care: Assess daily weight and I/O balance every 8 h
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and fluid overload signs
Check labs: BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, hemoglobin
Inspect skin and mucous membranes for pruritus or ulcers
Prepare patient for dialysis sessions and monitor access
patient_teaching: Low‑sodium diet (<2 g/day) and potassium per serum level
Limit fluid intake as prescribed (e.g., 1.5 L/day)
Take antihypertensives and erythropoietin as directed
Importance of regular dialysis attendance or transplant follow‑up

outcomes: Fluid balance: weight stable ±0.5 kg in 48 h
Edema reduced to mild level in 72 h

interventions.action: Record weight and I/O balance every 8 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes in fluid retention

interventions.action: Assess edema (pitting) and record scale
interventions.rationale: Monitors severity of fluid overload

interventions.action: Administer furosemide per order and observe response
interventions.rationale: Loop diuretic promotes excess Na⁺ and water excretion

interventions.action: Elevate patient’s legs when safe
interventions.rationale: Facilitates venous return and reduces peripheral edema

interventions.action: Educate patient on sodium and fluid restriction
interventions.rationale: Reduces intake contributing to retention

outcomes: Serum Na⁺ and K⁺ within normal ranges (Na⁺ 135‑145 mEq/L, K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) in 72 h

interventions.action: Monitor serum electrolytes and arterial gases every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early alterations and allows timely intervention

interventions.action: Assess neurological signs (confusion, muscle weakness)
interventions.rationale: Electrolyte imbalances may present neurologically

interventions.action: Administer calcium or phosphate supplements as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Corrects specific imbalances and prevents bone complications

interventions.action: Reinforce low‑potassium and low‑phosphorus diet education
interventions.rationale: Controls intake affecting serum levels

interventions.action: Adjust antihypertensive medication (ACE inhibitor/ARB) per labs
interventions.rationale: These drugs can raise K⁺ and may require adjustment

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to the Renal System

summary.0.quote: The disease course is complicated by hypertension, progressive loss of kidney function, and pain.

summary.1.quote: If your kidneys fail, you need treatment to replace the work they normally do.

key_points.1.quote: Common manifestations include proteinuria, decreased GFR, hypertension, and edema.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: SGLT2Is were primarily used to treat type 2 diabetes but recently were found to be useful in heart failure.

sections.treatment.4.quote: The treatment options are dialysis or a kidney transplant .

sections.complications.1.quote: A sodium-restricted diet (less than 2000 mg of sodium per day) may help maintain euvolemia (normal blood volume) and prevent clients from becoming overloaded with fluid (which presents as pitting edema in the extremities, abdominal edema, and/or pulmonary edema).
